findings.issue: REQ-008 (lines 263-282) is the new SSOT for paths: 'no default expansion ... callers must set ANICCA_HOME ... The loop never hard-codes ~/.anicca', and the config table at line 300 sets ANICCA_HOME = '(required — no default)'. But the rest of the spec was NOT reconciled to this. REQ-001 still hard-codes the genesis path '~/.anicca/identity/genesis.md' (line 47) and the ledger path '~/.anicca/state/ledger.jsonl' (lines 52, 35), REQ-009 hard-codes loading '~/.anicca/.env' (line 288), the Purity Boundary still names '~/.anicca/state/ledger.jsonl' (line 35), and verification-architecture.md:33 states dotenv.mjs does 'fs.readFile of ~/.anicca/.env'. These literal ~/.anicca paths directly contradict REQ-008's acceptance criterion (line 282: 'no hard-coded ~/.anicca ... literals; all paths derive from ANICCA_HOME'). An implementer cannot satisfy both REQ-001/REQ-009 (read ~/.anicca/...) and REQ-008 (never hard-code ~/.anicca) — the spec is internally contradictory and therefore not unambiguously implementable.

REQ-003 says the loop reads 'the NEW ledger line that run.sh appended to state/earn-ledger.jsonl' and applies isProfitable() (lines 123-125). But the spec never specifies HOW the loop obtains that single new line. run.sh writes to EARN_LEDGER (run.sh:41, default $HERE/state/earn-ledger.jsonl) via record.mjs (run.sh:55). The spec gives no contract for (a) which earn-ledger path the loop reads (it must match run.sh's EARN_LEDGER, which the loop is NOT shown to set), (b) how the loop identifies the line as 'new' (by WAKE_ID match? by tail? by line-count delta before/after?). isProfitable() (ledger.mjs:43-49) operates on one line object, so the loop must isolate exactly the line run.sh just wrote. Without a stated correlation key (e.g. match earn-ledger line.wake === WAKE_ID forwarded at run.sh:42), a concurrent or stale line could be mis-classified as the current wake's result. This is an under-specified earn-detection contract, the exact class of ambiguity Phase 1c must eliminate.

The most load-bearing new invariant — 'never claim earn without isProfitable() true on the real earn-ledger line' (behavioral-spec.md:155-157) — has NO proof obligation. PROP-020 (verification-architecture.md:60) only proves the 64-hex key-leak property over the observation/ledger string (REQ-004). REQ-003 in the REQ->PROP table (verification-architecture.md:120) maps ONLY to PROP-015 (skill-exit-nonzero) + PROP-020 (key leak). There is NO PROP asserting: (i) a profitable earn-ledger line (tx+0x1+net>0+external) -> loop records profitable:true, (ii) a narrate/discover/swap line (or exit 0 with no new line) -> loop records profitable:false, (iii) exit 0 alone never yields profitable:true (the acceptance at behavioral-spec.md:161-162). The classification logic the loop must implement around isProfitable() is asserted in prose but is unverifiable as written, so the central anti-false-earn invariant cannot be proven.

REQ-006 SIGTERM-during-running-skill-subprocess (behavioral-spec.md:174-177: SIGTERM child, wait up to 5s, exit) and its acceptance 'No orphan child processes remain' (line 229) remain unverified. PROP-013 (verification-architecture.md:53) only asserts the last ledger line is kind:'shutdown'; no PROP asserts the no-orphan-process post-condition or exercises the 5s child-kill timeout path, and the integration strategy (verification-architecture.md:90-99) spins up index.mjs against a mock HTTP server but never spawns a real long-running child to drive this branch. This was raised in iteration 1 and is still unaddressed; orphan-process leakage is a real cloud/durability hazard left unprovable.

overallNote: Three iteration-1 findings are confirmed RESOLVED with file:line evidence. The spec is NOT approvable: it has an internal path contradiction (REQ-001/REQ-009/Purity-Boundary hard-code ~/.anicca while REQ-008 forbids it), an under-specified earn-line correlation contract (no WAKE_ID/tail key for picking the new earn-ledger line), and the central never-claim-unverified-earn + SIGTERM-no-orphan invariants have no proof obligation in verification-architecture.md.
